steps.summary: Every size now belongs to one job on a nine-step ladder, the headline is sized from the column it fills, and four weights became three.

changes.what: The hero headline is sized from its column (18 characters a line) instead of the window, so it holds three even lines at every width and scales with zoom
Section headings came down to one fixed size so the hero stays the one loud moment, and the closing banner no longer competes with it
changes.before: clamp(30px, 3.4vw, 44px) at 700; closing heading clamp(32px, 4vw, 52px) at 700

changes.what: Body copy grew to the expressive range and card text joined it, so descriptions read as reading copy, not captions
changes.after: 17px for both, card copy separated by its grey tier and 1.5 leading

changes.what: Fourteen font sizes collapsed to nine, one per role
Nothing anyone reads sits below 12px any more, including the product mock's hour numbers on phones
changes.before: 11px labels and hour cells, 9.5px on phones

changes.what: Four font weights became three, each with one job, and two unused font files stopped downloading
changes.before: 400, 500, 600, 700 in use; Inter 500 and Inter Tight 500 requested
changes.after: 400 reading, 600 headings and controls, 700 the headline and wordmarks only

changes.what: Prices line up as columns and no longer outshout the section heading
The text no longer jumps when the web font arrives: each family falls back to a metric-matched local Arial
changes.after: Inter Fallback size-adjust 106.95%, Inter Tight Fallback 96%, with matched ascent and descent

steps.summary: Every colour became a named token, the four places that failed contrast now pass, and colour is no longer the only thing saying a state.

changes.what: The keyboard focus ring is visible on every surface it can land on
changes.after: #e2512a, 3.86:1 on white, 3.60:1 on the grey bands, 4.91:1 on dark; white (8.67:1) inside the closing banner

changes.what: Text on the orange accent switched from white to ink, so "Most popular", "Send invite" and the best-hour cells are readable
Orange section labels and icon strokes darkened until they pass as text
changes.before: #e2512a, 3.86:1 on white, 3.47:1 on the peach tile
changes.after: #c2410c, 5.18:1 on white, 4.66:1 on the peach tile

changes.what: The quietest grey now passes on the tinted bands too, and the customer logos use it
"Off" hours in the planner are readable and marked by a dashed outline, not by a faint grey alone
Green is kept for outcomes: the passed "Connected" step and the pricing ticks went neutral, and every done chip gained a check glyph
changes.before: 14 green ticks and 2 green chips; tick #12a26a on #e3f6ee, 2.92:1
changes.after: 1 green chip ("Invite sent"); ink ticks on grey discs, 17.17:1

changes.what: Teammate avatars moved off the hues that already mean something (the brand orange, the working-hours blue, success green)
changes.after: rose, violet, teal, slate — 4 named person colours

changes.what: Colour literals typed into rules became tokens named for their job
changes.before: 64 raw colours flagged by the detector

steps.summary: Spacing now runs on four named steps that group headings with their content, paragraphs share one reading width, and radii follow one ladder.

changes.what: Section rhythm opened up and each heading sits closer to its content than to the section before
Every intro and closing paragraph shares one reading width
Twelve corner radii became a four-step ladder
Chips and tags share one shape
On tablets and phones the section links move to a second header row instead of disappearing
changes.after: 4 links in a scrollable second row

changes.what: Jumping to a section no longer hides its heading under the sticky header
The focus ring got the expressive emphasis weight and the featured plan a firmer edge

steps.summary: Boxes are kept for things you choose — the plans and the closing banner — while features, steps, quotes and FAQs sit on the page.

changes.what: Bordered boxes below the hero dropped from 22 to 4
changes.before: 22 cards (6 features, 3 steps, 3 quotes, 3 plans, 6 FAQs, 1 banner)
changes.after: 4 (3 plans, 1 banner); features parted by space, steps and quotes by a top hairline, FAQs by row rules

changes.what: Flat things lost their shadows: buttons, the announcement pill and the steps
changes.before: 5 shadowed flat elements, primary button shadow at 50% opacity

changes.what: Three shadow recipes became one per level, from one light, and the strongest is gentler
changes.after: 2: raised (peak 10%) and floating (contact + 2 ambient + highlight, peak 16%)

changes.what: The translucent header starts opaque and only turns to glass where the browser supports it, with paths for reduced transparency, high contrast and forced colours
changes.before: no @supports guard, no preference fallbacks; blur 14px
changes.after: opaque baseline + @supports; blur 20px, saturate 1.8; 3 preference blocks

changes.what: The best-hour cell's orange drop glow is gone; fill and weight mark it

steps.summary: Motion now explains a change or doesn't happen: one looping animation and one hover lift went, and every timing comes from a short ladder.

changes.what: The suggestion card stopped bobbing up and down forever
Timings come from a ladder sized by how much changes
changes.after: 120ms colour, 200ms button fill, 280ms FAQ marker opening, 180ms closing

changes.what: Buttons answer the press at once with a scale instead of a 1px nudge
The FAQ plus closes faster and flatter than it opens
changes.after: opens 280ms with slight overshoot, closes 180ms ease-in

changes.what: Reduced motion keeps each signal instead of switching everything off
changes.before: global animation: none and transition: none on every element
changes.after: per component: instant scrolling, a flat 200ms FAQ turn, colour fades kept

steps.summary: Buttons and links now do what they say: the hero's play icon promised a video that doesn't exist, and the email address now opens an email.

changes.what: The secondary hero button lost a play icon that promised a video; it scrolls to the steps
The support email in the FAQ opens an email instead of going nowhere
Customer logos no longer darken on hover, since they aren't links
